text:
We do not carry it in dark amulets,

nor write rapturous sighs about it,

it does not disturb our bitter sleep,

nor seem to us the promised paradise.

In our soul we do not turn it

into an object bought or sold.

For it, sick, destitute, wandering,

we do not even remember it.


Yes, for us it is dirt on our shoes.

Yes, for us it is grit between our teeth.

And we grind, tear out, crush

that earth that mixes with nothing.

But in it we lie and we are it,

and therefore, happy, we call it ours.

translation.title: Native Land
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the unsentimental homeland as dirt, grit, burial ground, and identity.
